body.statement: Under complete randomization, \(\mathbb E W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)\le\tfrac12\sqrt{\rho_a}\) and \(W_1(G_a,\widehat F_a)\le N^{-1}\). For the quantile-lifted triple \(G\), \(|L_N(G)-L_N(F)|\le D_N(F,G)/(N-1)\) and \(\max\{|U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-U_N(F)|,|U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(F)|\}\le[D_N(F,G)+3456/N]/(N-1)\), with \(\mathbb ED_N(F,G)\le M_N\). If \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\), all three endpoint estimates have error \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-3/2})+O(N^{-2})\). For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the computable interval \([U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-[M_N/\eta+3456/N]/(N-1),U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)+[M_N/\eta+3456/N]/(N-1)]\) covers \(U_N(F)\) with probability at least \(1-\eta\).
body.justification: The sampling result separates armwise observation error from the smaller deterministic realization error and remains valid at ties and nonunique transport optima.
body.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014) establish consistent two-arm sharp-bound estimators, and Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) analyze superpopulation fractional plug-ins; neither treats a three-arm realizable endpoint under dependent sampling without replacement.
body.consumer: The result gives a conservative finite-sample uncertainty band for the sharp variance endpoint when no experiment reveals all three population marginals.
